requirement: A macOS desktop app (Tauri 2) opens the board in a native window and keeps running independently of Claude Code sessions
The app starts/supervises one board daemon per user; if a daemon is already running it attaches to it
Operational state is stored in an embedded SQLite DB in the app-data folder: projects, runs, run events, hand-offs, approvals, terminal sessions; schema versioned with forward migrations
The app lists projects and switches between them; the MCP server registers its project with the daemon on start
Specs, tickets, statuses and checkboxes remain markdown in `<project>/.SDD/specs/`; the DB never becomes their source of truth and can be deleted without losing work
Cards can be dragged between columns; move buttons remain as the keyboard alternative
A human move to a working stage records a hand-off (ticket, from, to, actor, time)

The MCP server delivers the hand-off into its session as `notifications/claude/channel` (fixed template naming ticket, stage and the skill to run) and declares `experimental.claude/channel` with `instructions`
Delivery is confirmed only when Claude calls a kanban tool for that hand-off (`kanban_start`); unconfirmed hand-offs stay 'queued' on the board

Fallback: if no channel session picks a hand-off up within a timeout (or the user clicks 'Run headless'), the daemon runs `claude -p --output-format stream-json` in the project, resuming the ticket's stored session id
At most one live run per ticket; duplicate hand-offs while queued/running are coalesced; a second run is refused
Moves made by Claude through MCP tools never produce a hand-off back to Claude
New MCP tools `kanban_start` (claim ticket/PRD, optional hand-off id), `kanban_heartbeat` (note), `kanban_finish` (outcome, summary)
Cards and sub-tasks with a queued/running run show an animated indicator plus text ('working · Architect · 12 s ago'); runs without a heartbeat past the TTL show 'stale', never 'working'
Ticket drawer shows run history and a live transcript for headless runs (streamed from stream-json), with a Stop button that terminates the run's process group
Embedded terminal per project (PTY), which can start `claude` with the kanban channel flag preset
Spec viewer/editor: render and edit the ticket's markdown files (writes confined to `.SDD/specs/`), and show a diff of spec files since the recorded approval
Read-only git panel: branch, changed/staged files for the project, and the latest hand-off git block; no git write actions
Leaving Approval for Developer requires a confirm dialog; the approval (approver, time, sha256 of the spec files) is written to the ticket README and the DB
A chat request to move or approve a ticket is handled by a skill that calls `kanban_move` / `kanban_approve`, recording the same approval with actor 'chat'

Skill `kanban:sdd`: create or continue the ticket for an issue, run Discovery → Architect writing spec files into it with self-contained templates, keep status current, stop at Approval; hand later stages to the project `sdd` skill when installed
`kanban:ticket` remains and routes to `kanban:sdd`; the `kanban` skill documents channel events, run tools and approval
The kit installer can build and install the app locally (`--only kanban-app`), checking prerequisites and printing what is missing
Without the app or daemon, the plugin keeps today's behaviour (MCP tools + embedded web board)
Runtime dependencies: the daemon, MCP server and skills stay Python 3.9+ standard library only. Build-time only: Rust (stable) and Node ≥ 18 for the Tauri shell

requirement: Security: daemon listens on `127.0.0.1` only, Host-header check, a per-install random token required for every write and for terminal/run endpoints (the terminal is remote code execution if exposed), CSP kept strict; file access confined to registered projects' `.SDD/specs/` except the PTY
Prompt-injection hygiene: channel content and headless prompts use fixed templates; ticket titles/paths passed as quoted data; only events originating from the local board are forwarded
Headless runs obey the project's `.claude/settings.json` and guard hook; no `--dangerously-skip-permissions`; permission mode per Q06
Performance: board renders ≤ 200 ms for 10 tickets × 50 PRDs; live updates via SSE (polling fallback), no busy loops
Resilience: if channels, the daemon, the DB or the app fail, Claude keeps working by editing markdown; a deleted DB is rebuilt empty without data loss
No regressions: `plugins/kanban/tests/test_kanban.py` and `tests/test_install.py` stay green; new Python code covered by stdlib `unittest`; Tauri shell covered by `cargo test` + a smoke launch
